title: 186. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Compound Linear Inequalities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a double inequality by subtracting the same number from all parts.
questions.question: Solve the compound inequality \(-1 < x+2 \le 5\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(2\) from all three parts of the inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-1-2 &< x+2-2 \le 5-2\\
-3 &< x \le 3
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-3 < x \le 3\).
questions.hint: Subtract the same number from each part of the double inequality.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an "and" compound inequality by finding the intersection of two inequalities.
questions.question: Solve \(2x-1 \ge 3\) and \(x+4 < 7\).
questions.explanation:
Solve each inequality separately.
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x-1 \ge 3 &\implies 2x \ge 4 \implies x \ge 2\\
x+4 < 7 &\implies x < 3
\end{aligned}
\]
The intersection of \(x \ge 2\) and \(x < 3\) is
\[
2 \le x < 3
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(2 \le x < 3\).
questions.hint: Solve each inequality separately, then find the values that satisfy both.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an "or" compound inequality by finding the union of two inequalities.
questions.question: Solve \(3x+2 < 11\) or \(x-1 \ge 4\).
questions.explanation:
Solve each inequality separately.
\[
\begin{aligned}
3x+2 < 11 &\implies 3x < 9 \implies x < 3\\
x-1 \ge 4 &\implies x \ge 5
\end{aligned}
\]
The solution is the union of these two sets:
\[
x < 3 \text{ or } x \ge 5
\]
Therefore, the correct choice is \(x < 3\) or \(x \ge 5\).
questions.hint: For "or", combine all values that satisfy at least one of the inequalities.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a three-part inequality by applying inverse operations to all parts.
questions.question: Solve \(-2 \le 3x+1 < 7\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(1\) from all three parts, then divide all three parts by \(3\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
-2-1 &\le 3x+1-1 < 7-1\\
-3 &\le 3x < 6\\
-1 &\le x < 2
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-1 \le x < 2\).
questions.hint: Apply the same inverse operations to every part of the inequality.

questions.concept: Compound Inequality with Variables on Both Sides
questions.learningObjective: Solve an "and" compound inequality involving variables on both sides.
questions.question: Solve \(4x-3 < 2x+5\) and \(x+1 \ge 0\).
questions.explanation:
Solve the first inequality, then solve the second inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
4x-3 < 2x+5 &\implies 2x < 8 \implies x < 4\\
x+1 \ge 0 &\implies x \ge -1
\end{aligned}
\]
The intersection of \(x < 4\) and \(x \ge -1\) is
\[
-1 \le x < 4
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-1 \le x < 4\).
questions.hint: Solve each inequality, then keep only the values that satisfy both.

questions.concept: Compound Inequality with a Negative Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Solve an "and" compound inequality and reverse the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number.
questions.question: Solve \(5-2x \ge 1\) and \(x+3 > 0\).
questions.explanation:
Solve the first inequality, then solve the second inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
5-2x \ge 1 &\implies -2x \ge -4 \implies x \le 2\\
x+3 > 0 &\implies x > -3
\end{aligned}
\]
The intersection is
\[
-3 < x \le 2
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-3 < x \le 2\).
questions.hint: Remember to reverse the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number.

questions.concept: "Or" Compound Inequality with All Real Solutions
questions.learningObjective: Determine when an "or" compound inequality is satisfied by all real numbers.
questions.question: Solve \(3(x-2) \le 2x+1\) or \(x-5 > -2\).
questions.explanation:
Solve the first inequality, then solve the second inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
3(x-2) \le 2x+1 &\implies 3x-6 \le 2x+1 \implies x \le 7\\
x-5 > -2 &\implies x > 3
\end{aligned}
\]
The solution is the union:
\[
x \le 7 \text{ or } x > 3
\]
Every real number satisfies at least one of these conditions, so the solution is all real numbers. Therefore, the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Solve each inequality separately, then combine the two solution sets, keeping every value that satisfies at least one of them.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an "and" compound inequality and express the intersection as an interval.
questions.question: Solve \(2x+1 < 5\) and \(3x-2 \ge -8\).
questions.explanation:
Solve the first inequality, then solve the second inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x+1 < 5 &\implies 2x < 4 \implies x < 2\\
3x-2 \ge -8 &\implies 3x \ge -6 \implies x \ge -2
\end{aligned}
\]
The intersection is
\[
-2 \le x < 2
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-2 \le x < 2\).
questions.hint: Solve each inequality and keep only the overlap of the two solution sets.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a three-part linear inequality with a positive coefficient.
questions.question: Solve \(-3 < 2x-1 \le 5\).
questions.explanation:
Add \(1\) to all three parts, then divide all three parts by \(2\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
-3+1 &< 2x-1+1 \le 5+1\\
-2 &< 2x \le 6\\
-1 &< x \le 3
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(-1 < x \le 3\).
questions.hint: Add the same number to each part, then divide each part by the same positive number.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an "or" compound inequality and simplify the union of the solution sets.
questions.question: Solve \(-x+2 \ge 5\) or \(2x+3 < 1\).
questions.explanation:
Solve the first inequality, then solve the second inequality:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-x+2 \ge 5 &\implies -x \ge 3 \implies x \le -3\\
2x+3 < 1 &\implies 2x < -2 \implies x < -1
\end{aligned}
\]
The union is
\[
x \le -3 \text{ or } x < -1
\]
Since every number less than or equal to \(-3\) is already less than \(-1\), the union simplifies to
\[
x < -1
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x < -1\).
questions.hint: After finding the union, simplify it by checking whether one solution set is contained in the other.
